title: Fujitsu Japan uses AI to streamline clinical trial recruitment in Japan | HealthCare Middle East & Africa - No.1 Health & Pharma Manufacturing Industry Publication

contentHtml:
JAPAN – Fujitsu Japan Limited, the National Cancer Center Hospital East (NCCHE), and US-based Paradigm Health has completed joint research demonstrating how artificial intelligence (AI) can accelerate the identification of patients eligible for clinical trials.

The study, conducted between June and October 2026 at NCCHE, used an AI-powered approach to screen patient records and identify potential candidates for new drug trials.

The research combined a large language model (LLM) with Paradigm Health’s clinical trial matching platform, known as Paradigm Platform.

It assessed data from 22,334 patients in the hospital’s Department of Respiratory Medicine, using a simulated clinical trial targeting patients with EGFR gene mutations.

AI reduces clinical trial screening workload

As part of the study, Fujitsu Japan anonymised and processed electronic medical records from 3,027 lung cancer patients using an LLM to structure information on medical histories, treatments and genomic profiles.

The resulting data were then integrated into the Paradigm Platform for eligibility assessment.

Paradigm evaluated 540 patients with EGFR mutations against five clinical trial eligibility criteria.

The system identified 57 priority candidates and provided supporting clinical evidence for each selection.

A subsequent review by physicians confirmed that 51 of the identified patients were promising candidates for clinical trials.

Traditionally, identifying suitable participants has required physicians and clinical research coordinators to manually examine medical records, treatment histories and laboratory results.

This process can be time-consuming, particularly as precision medicine introduces increasingly complex eligibility requirements based on genetic mutations and biomarkers.

The AI-assisted approach enabled automated overnight screening and reduced the number of patient records requiring manual review by approximately 89%.

This could ease administrative workloads, accelerate recruitment and allow clinical research teams to focus on evaluating patients with a higher likelihood of meeting trial requirements.

Fujitsu targets commercialisation by 2027

Following the research, Fujitsu Japan plans to commercialise a service supporting the entire clinical trial recruitment process, from initial patient screening to enrolment.

The company is targeting a launch by the end of fiscal year 2027 and intends to promote adoption across medical institutions in Japan.

The initiative addresses Japan’s drug loss challenge, in which medicines available in other markets are not developed or approved domestically.

Complex recruitment procedures and fragmented medical records can delay clinical trials, limiting opportunities for patients to access emerging therapies.

The challenge also extends to international research.

Differences in medical data formats and the prevalence of unstructured information in Japanese electronic health records make it difficult to integrate patient information into global clinical research systems.

By combining LLM-based data processing with an established clinical trial matching platform, the partnership seeks to make patient identification more consistent and improve the use of clinical data in research.

The initiative forms part of Fujitsu Japan’s Uvance business model, which uses AI and digital technologies to support business transformation and address societal challenges.

The company is extending this approach to healthcare, with a focus on improving clinical trial operations and expanding access to investigational treatments.
